note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Ezekiel says the same: “And I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries: according to their way and according to their doings I judged them.”

They're dispersed. Israel was scattered among the heathen and dispersed through the countries, judged according to their own ways and doings. The Pharisees and chief priests understood Ezekiel 36 and the dispersed, along with Isaiah 11 and Tobit 3. So when they asked, “Whither will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?”, they were speaking of scattered Israel living among the heathen.

note.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

precepts.why:
Ezekiel 36:24-28 is the Lord changing us: gathered out of all countries, sprinkled with clean water, which is the commandments of God, given a new heart, a new mind, a new body, a new nervous system, with the stony, sinful heart that Adam had taken away. Then verse 33 shows what comes next: “Thus saith the Lord God; In the day that I shall have cleansed you from all your iniquities I will also cause you to dwell in the cities, and the wastes shall be builded.”

“And the desolate land shall be tilled, whereas it lay desolate in the sight of all that passed by. And they shall say, This land that was desolate is become like the garden of Eden”. First the Lord changes you; now he changes the land to conform to you. The Lord made it for us; the world was made for us. But he can't give us Jerusalem the way it is supposed to be right now, because we are in the midst of sin.

So he says: let me remove the sin, let me cleanse you, let me give you a new heart, let me remove that weak, brittle body and give you immortality. Then he will command the land to transform into the garden of Eden. We are going right back to where we were in the beginning with our father Adam, and we are going to be with our father Adam again: his name is Jesus the Christ, the black Messiah, in the same place.

“and the waste and desolate and ruined cities are become fenced, and are inhabited. Then the heathen that are left round about you shall know that I the Lord build the ruined places, and plant that that was desolate: I the Lord have spoken it, and I will do it.” The nations will say, God is with these people. He has spoken it, and he will do it.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
Ezekiel tells why the real 12 tribes were removed: “when the house of Israel dwelt in their own land, they defiled it by their own way and by their doings: their way was before me as the uncleanness of a removed woman.” We defiled our land by our own ways, like a menstruous woman; that is how disgusted God was with us, and he had to remove us out of the land. “Wherefore I poured my fury upon them for the blood that they had shed upon the land, and for their idols wherewith they had polluted it: And I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries”.

James writes to that same people: “James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.” The New Testament letter is addressed to the 12 tribes, scattered abroad, exactly as Ezekiel said they would be. I don't know why a Christian can't understand this.

And once scattered, “when they entered unto the heathen, whither they went, they profaned my holy name, when they said to them, These are the people of the Lord, and are gone forth out of his land.” How do we profane God's holy name? We started to say, y'all are the Jews now, we're not the Jews. We started to call the white man Jews. So that is the prophecy of what is going on today: the real black Jews saying to the white man, y'all are the Jews, y'all are God's chosen people.

So the real Israel is the people scattered among the nations, the twelve tribes James wrote to, not the ones who took the land with despiteful minds and called their European friends to come and get a part of it.

precepts.text: In the fire of my jealousy have I spoken against the residue of the heathen and against all Idumea, which have appointed my land into their possession with the joy of all their heart, with despiteful minds, to cast it out for a prey. No text says Japheth lives in the land; Idumea does. They took it knowing it was not theirs and called their fellow Idumeans from Poland, Russia, Germany, and Ukraine to take a part, which is why they speak with those accents.
precepts.point: In 1948 they got the land again, set up schools, and taught a new Hebrew. Biblical Hebrew was extinct from 70 AD; the father of modern Hebrew fused French, Arabic, Aramaic, Spanish, and German words, and now Negroes argue over it. They got the land, made a language, called themselves Jewish, and the prophecy says they shall fall.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
“Surely in the fire of my jealousy have I spoken against the residue of the heathen, and against all Idumea, which have appointed my land into their possession”. This verse, along with Ezekiel 35:12, identifies the race that would live in the land. It doesn't say Japheth. There is no biblical text that says Japheth lives in the land. The Bible says Idumea would take and live in the land.

“with the joy of all their heart”: they were happy to steal, to spoil the land. “with despiteful minds”: they took the land despite knowing the land doesn't belong to them, despite the fact they're not the Jews.

“to cast it out for a prey”: they called their fellow Idumeans from Poland, Russia, Germany, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Ukraine and said, come, take a part, and a lot of them came. That is why, if you listen to them speak, they speak German, Polish and Russian with those accents. They are not the people of the land.

That is the vision the robbers of thy people exalt themselves to establish in Daniel 11:14, and God has spoken against all Idumea in the fire of his jealousy. They shall fall.

precepts.text: The desolate land shall be tilled and become like the garden of Eden, and when Israel learns the law they shall lothe themselves in their own sight for their iniquities; I the Lord have spoken it, and I will do it.
precepts.point: The Most High says he will return the land to its original form, like the garden of Eden; that is a precept in itself, for the garden of Eden is Jerusalem, the land of Israel, the land of milk and honey.

note.label: Deuteronomy 8: Keep the Commandments and Live

precepts.why:
Verses 7 through 9 are the precept for describing the land of milk and honey: “a good land, a land of brooks of water, of fountains and depths that spring out of valleys and hills; A land of wheat, and barley, and vines, and fig trees, and pomegranates; a land of oil olive, and honey”, where “thou shalt eat bread without scarceness”, whose stones are iron and out of whose hills thou mayest dig brass. Write it down and use it.

Right now the land is not flowing with milk and honey: the place is desolate, full of desert places, and much of its food is imported, exactly as the prophecy requires until the Most High restores it. Ezekiel gives the restoring: “I will call for the corn, and will increase it, and lay no famine upon you. And I will multiply the fruit of the tree, and the increase of the field, that ye shall receive no more reproach of famine among the heathen.”

“And the desolate land shall be tilled, whereas it lay desolate in the sight of all that passed by. And they shall say, This land that was desolate is become like the garden of Eden”. The Most High says he will return the land to its original form, like the garden of Eden; that is a precept in itself, for the garden of Eden is Jerusalem, the land of Israel, the land of milk and honey.

And when Israel learns the law: “Then shall ye remember your own evil ways, and your doings that were not good, and shall lothe yourselves in your own sight for your iniquities and for your abominations.” “Not for your sakes do I this, saith the Lord God”. It is sure: “I the Lord have spoken it, and I will do it.”

That is what the Most High did for Saul: “when he had turned his back to go from Samuel, God gave him another heart: and all those signs came to pass that day.”

This is the diaspora, the same scattering some now call the African diaspora.
